description:
FILED s465az (Opus, round 23).  Two companion files disagree with
baselines/perl-suite-run.tsv on a QUIET box and were NOT spliced, because
"pre-existing is WHEN, not why" (ruled s421) and neither has a cause yet.
Both were re-measured ALONE after the parallel `--all`; the other NINE movers
of that run were LOAD and reproduced the snapshot exactly (io/through.t and
io/crlf_through.t are OK 942/0 alone, io/open.t 154/34, re/charset.t
2776/2775, op/cond.t 4/1, io/pvbm.t 20/8).

(a) comp/require.t   snapshot DIFF 909/835  ->  910/837  (measured 3x: the
    --all parallel, the #366 serial re-run, and a named run alone)
    THREE ROWS GAINED, none lost.  The file is TIME-BOUNDED: it does not
    finish, it is cut off at its registered 450 s allowance
    (baselines/perl-suite-timeouts.tsv: "genuinely SLOW, not hung"), so its row
    count is a function of machine speed and this may be nothing but a faster
    box.  DISCRIMINATING MEASUREMENT, not taken here: run it at --timeout 900
    on a quiet box and see whether the count keeps climbing.  If it does, the
    snapshot row is a clock reading and should say so; if it plateaus at
    910/837, splice it with that cause.

(b) re/overload.t    snapshot TIMEOUT 3/0  ->  TIMEOUT 0/0  (measured 2x: the
    --all parallel and alone)
    THREE PASSING ROWS LOST.  This is a #326 hang-set file: `--quick` never
    runs it and the last recorded measurement is s404 ("3 of perl's 87 rows at
    90 s, at 300 s and at 900 s").  It is now stamped in
    baselines/perl-suite-notrun-stamps.tsv, which is how the age of this kind
    of hole becomes visible at all.
    WORTH A LOOK BECAUSE OF WHAT IT IS: an overload file losing its first
    three rows in the round that changed overload dispatch (#972, round 22)
    and tail-return (#994, round 23) is a coincidence worth one probe.  The
    cheap discriminator: run `tools/run-perl-suite.pl re/overload.t` on a
    worktree at `ea34c0f` and at `1fed80b` and compare â 3 rows either way is
    the answer.  A plausible innocent cause is buffering: the file is KILLED
    at the timeout, so whether its first rows reach the pipe depends on when
    SBCL flushes.

NEITHER was spliced into baselines/perl-suite-run.tsv.  A mover joins the
snapshot with its cause, not with its date.
subject: Two companion snapshot movers measured on a QUIET box and NOT spliced: comp/require.t 909/835 -> 910/837 (a time-bounded file: 3 rows gained) and re/overload.t TIMEOUT 3/0 -> 0/0 (3 passing rows lost in an OVERLOAD file, one round after the overload work) â each carries its discriminating measurement
